Q: What goes wrong with a mutable default argument in Python?
spoken: Default argument expressions are evaluated when the function is defined. A default list can therefore retain additions across calls. Use None as the sentinel and create a new list inside the function when a fresh collection is intended. Sometimes persistent shared state is deliberate, but it should be explicit and synchronized if accessed concurrently.

Q: When should a Python interface use an iterator instead of constructing a list?
spoken: An iterator yields values as they are requested and can avoid retaining the entire result. It may be single-use and can defer errors until iteration. A list supports repeated traversal and indexed access but retains its elements. Streaming is useful only when downstream consumers do not immediately materialize the whole iterator.
A:
An iterator yields values as they are requested and can avoid retaining the entire result. It may be single-use and can defer errors until iteration. A list supports repeated traversal and indexed access but retains its elements. Streaming is useful only when downstream consumers do not immediately materialize the whole iterator.
